result.answer:
**Transformer 1, MAIN:** The available window is **15–19 January 2024**, with five daily records—not current telemetry. All 20 channels you specified have **5/5 numeric values**; none is empty.

The table covers all nine stored failure modes; the catalog is marked non-exhaustive. Coverage means diagnostic observability, not evidence that a fault exists.

| Known failure mode | Most diagnostic channels from your list | Coverage | Interpretation / gap-closing test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Partial Discharge in Oil | `hydrogen`, `methane`, `acetylene` | well covered | Hydrogen-dominant gas pattern, methane/hydrogen relationship, and little acetylene help distinguish PD from arcing. Electrical/acoustic PD testing confirms it. |
| Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating | `methane`, `ethane`, `ethylene` | well covered | Relative thermal-gas production distinguishes lower- from higher-temperature oil decomposition. |
| Thermal Fault — Core/Winding | `ethylene`, `ethane`, `co` | partially covered | Thermal-gas pattern detects heating; CO supports possible paper involvement. It cannot localize core versus winding. Add excitation-current/core-ground testing and winding-resistance testing during an outage. |
| Low-Energy Arcing (Sparking) | `acetylene`, `hydrogen`, `ethylene` | well covered | Their combined pattern helps discriminate electrical discharge and its energy class; no single gas is sufficient. |
| High-Energy Arcing | `acetylene`, `ethylene`, `hydrogen` | well covered | Acetylene with the ethylene/hydrogen pattern supports high-energy discharge discrimination. Confirm with repeat laboratory DGA and protection-event evidence. |
| Tap Changer Mechanical Wear | **None genuinely discriminatory** | blind | Main-tank gases and phase currents cannot establish mechanical wear; switching can normally generate gases. Use tap-changer inspection, operating timing/motor-current signature and dynamic resistance testing. |
| Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress | `dielectric_rigidity`, `interfacial_v` | partially covered | Breakdown strength and interfacial tension screen contamination effects, but cannot identify moisture specifically. Add Karl Fischer moisture and particle-count tests on a fresh oil sample. |
| Cellulose Insulation Ageing | `co`, `co2` | partially covered | Their trends and relationship support cellulose degradation screening, but oil oxidation also produces them. Add oil furan analysis, especially 2-FAL; paper degree-of-polymerization testing where accessible. |
| Oil Dielectric Degradation | `dielectric_rigidity`, `interfacial_v` | well covered | Direct breakdown-strength measurement plus interfacial tension tracks dielectric deterioration and polar degradation products. Laboratory breakdown voltage, acidity and dissipation-factor tests provide confirmation. |

**Limits:** `interfacial_v` is interpreted as oil interfacial tension. I have not padded the selections with load currents, ambient temperature or alarm flags: they provide context, not mode discrimination. Likewise, DBDS indicates corrosive-sulfur risk—not generic dielectric degradation.

No mode is blind **because of an empty channel** in this window. Tap-changer wear is blind because suitable measurements are absent from the requested set. `water_content` also has data outside your shortlist, so moisture coverage could improve if that channel’s units and validity are confirmed. **Fresh telemetry and oil samples are needed for present-day planning.**
